text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High severity: multiple CUDA OOMs on serving-runtime pool 'infer-gpu-pool' (node: infer-03). 5xx spike on /v1/generate, ~18% error rate for the last 3m. Detected: runtime reported cudaErrorMemoryAllocation during model forward despite ~12GB free reported by nvidia-smi on GPU0. Auto-page to oncall. https://internal/alerts/1768604123

ryan: acked. I'm paged and will start triage. any obvious customer-facing degradations?

zoe: CS: seeing multiple customers showing failed requests, some retries hitting fallback CPU and increased latency. Not yet widespread but a high-traffic ML customer reports 40% failures.

claire: joining. quick question — are these new nodes or a long-running host?

ryan: infer-03 has been up for ~12d, running a mix of host and dedicated sessions. No recent deploys to runtime in the last 30m per deploy-bot.

aditya: likelihood: allocator fragmentation or reserved-blocks leak. PyTorch runtime sometimes can't service a contiguous allocation even when total free memory looks OK. We saw similar symptoms before where reserved bytes >> active bytes.

matt: pulling logs. runtime stderr shows repeated: 
```
E tensorflow: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory at /src/runtime/allocator.cu:214
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2147483648 bytes.
Allocator stats: reserved_bytes=12884787200 allocated_bytes=1092372480 max_cached_bytes=8589934592
```

zoe: (customer impact) two customers on dedicated capacity affected. they're open to temporary reroute to dedicated backup.

claire: can someone run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.free --format=csv` on infer-03? also `python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"` in a debug shell against the runtime container.

ryan: running now, attaching output:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
index, memory.used [MiB], memory.free [MiB]
0, 3072 MiB, 12288 MiB
```
and from Python (trimmed):
```
| allocated  | 1100 MiB |
| reserved   | 12280 MiB |
| active allocs | 24 |
| reserved blocks | 15 (avg 816 MiB) |
```

aditya: confirmed: reserved >> allocated and reserved blocks are large (~800MB each). Fragmentation likely. The runtime's caching/reservation is holding large slabs. New allocations for large tensors fail because contiguous slab not free even though total free looks big.

matt: two quick mitigation options: 1) restart the runtime container on infer-03 to flush GPU cache (fast, service impact for in-flight requests), 2) try to force allocator to return cached memory by toggling environment flags on the running process (harder).

claire: prefer non-disruptive first — can we reduce batch size / token limit for requests routed to infer-03 to avoid large single allocations? routing change can be applied in the router for ~10m while we stabilize.

ryan: scaling policy: temporarily shift ~30% traffic away from infer-03 using smart-routing (tag-based fallback to infer-01/02), applying a canary. Doing that now.

incident-bot: action: routed 30% of traffic away from infer-03 to infer-01/02 at 17:05 UTC.

aditya: still seeing OOMs for requests routed to infer-03 that require large context windows. mitigation idea: set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` or reduce `reserved_block_size` in runtime config to lower max slab size — this allows allocator to split larger requests instead of single huge reserved blocks. We can also temporarily set `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=2000000000` to shrink KV cache per model.

matt: I can patch the container env and hot-restart the worker process (graceful child restart) without container restart. That should drop cached reserved blocks. doing that in 1m: `kubectl exec -n infra infer-03 -- pkill -HUP redwood-runtime-worker` after setting env.

ryan: please confirm expected client impact for pkill -HUP.

matt: HUP triggers worker reload to new env; in-flight sessions may fail for requests hitting that worker; routing already reduced to 30% so blast radius small.

claire: runbook step: if HUP doesn't free memory, escalate to full container restart and node drain. 

matt: applied env changes in pod spec: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` and `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=2000000000`, then SIGHUP to worker. logs: 
```
[17:18:22] worker: reloaded config, clearing per-process caches
[17:18:23] cuda: freed 9.7 GiB from reserved cache
[17:18:25] worker: warmup done, accepting requests
```

aditya: nice. monitoring error rate.

ryan: error rate on /v1/generate for infer-03 dropping from 18% -> 3% over 5m. nvidia-smi now shows reserved down:
```
0, memory.used 2890 MiB, memory.free 12400 MiB
```

zoe: customer update: telling impacted customers we've mitigated and are running follow-up root cause analysis; no data was lost.

claire: logging short-term postmortem tasks: 1) add runtime guard to prevent reserved_block > 256MB default, 2) add auto-trigger to reduce routing if OOM spike on a single node > 5% of requests, 3) add more detailed allocator metrics to telemetry (reserved_blocks_count, largest_free_block). I'll file follow-ups.

aditya: also recommending kernel-level defragmentation attempt for the allocator in next runtime build and a fix to release reserved blocks after long idle periods. I'll put up a PR with tests.

matt: for this incident I restarted the worker and applied env changes; no further restarts required. I've left a snapshot of logs and the exact patch in the incident ticket.

ryan: handing off to claire for next 4h mitigation/harden work. taking us to lower priority monitoring.

claire: handover acked. I'll own the follow-ups and customer comms for the next 4h. tagging @aditya for the runtime patch.

incident-bot: [RESOLVED] Alert resolved at 17:52 UTC. Incident duration ~47m. Follow-ups created in backlog: RED-1423 (allocator fragmentation fix), RED-1424 (allocator telemetry), RED-1425 (routing auto-throttle).

zoe: closing loop with customers and scheduling a postmortem doc for tomorrow 09:00 PT.

claire: short postmortem notes in ticket: root cause probable allocator fragmentation + oversized reserved-blocks + KV cache not trimming; immediate mitigation was env tweak + worker reload + routing diversion. Long-term: change default reserved block size and add telemetry + regression tests.

ryan: thanks team. great quick coord. :thumbsup:
